newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Rwanda does not back Boutros-Ghali -ambassador.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda does not back Boutros-Ghali -ambassador.

text.p: Rwanda's ambassador to Belgium said on Tuesday his country did not back Boutros Boutros-Ghali for another term as United Nations secretary general and would support another African candidate instead.
"The Rwandan government is not in favour of Boutros Boutros-Ghali's re-election. I don't think it would bring much to the African continent," Manzi Bakuramutsa told a news conference.
He blamed the Egyptian secretary-general for ineffective management of the African crises that have blown up since he has held the post, and accused him of sometimes showing a lack of neutrality.
At the time of Rwanda's 1994 genocide the United Nations did not intervene until it was too late, he added.
"We're waiting for the candidates to come forward and we are expecting an African one, as it is Africa's turn for the post," Bakuramutsa added.
Boutros-Ghali's term expires on December 31, and on Monday the United States was the only voice in the 15-member Security Council opposing his re-election.

The Rwandan ambassador also joined calls for the international community to focus its interest in the Great Lakes region not on eastern Zaire but on resettling the tide of Rwandan refugees flooding back home from camps there.

"It's logical to take help to where the refugees are now. Planes that were going to carry troops should bring aid," he said, adding supplies of food and shelter were needed for three months to help reintegrate the returnees.

Plans to intervene in eastern Zaire with a Canadian-led multinational humanitarian task force have come under question by many countries now that an estimated 500,000 Rwandan Hutus have returned home from Zaire's Tutsi rebel-held Goma region.

However aid workers say at least as many refugees are still at risk in Zaire's Bukavu region, and the French and British governments have said they remain committed to sending troops to help with the humanitarian crisis.
Official estimates put at over one million the number of mostly Hutu refugees who have been living in camps in eastern Zaire for two years since fleeing Rwanda's genocide.
But Rwanda insists almost all have now left Zaire.

The ambassador said the Rwandan government was able to organise the distribution of aid it received. Returning refugees would be given the right to the property they had left behind, and Rwandan authorities would settle any disputes.
